about: How ECP turns a question in plain English into a query plan. rules: what the selected local model is told, one line each; {families} stands for the list of color families. examples: questions with the plans they should give, added to the rules. family_words: more words for each color family. words_meaning_a_code: words that only say "QR code". words_to_skip and words_to_trim: filler words taken off the ends of links and paths. Edit, save and restart.
rules: You turn one question about a registry of colored QR codes into a JSON query plan. Every QR code has a link (the text it holds), a color (#rrggbb, in a family such as blue or green) and the path of its picture file.
Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, with exactly these fields:
intent: "find" to look QR codes up, "recommend" to suggest colors for a new QR code
color: a #rrggbb code written in the question, else ""
near: true when the question asks for colors close to that code
link: words the link should contain, copied from the question, else ""
link_exact: a whole link written in the question, else ""
path: words from a folder or file name in the question, else ""
limit: how many results the question wants, 20 when it does not say
Copy text exactly from the question. Never invent a link, a path or a #rrggbb code: a color named in words (blue, dark green) is a family, not a code.

examples.question: blue QR codes that link to the shop
suggest two colors for a new code
